newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Scott says may match or beat 95/96 net.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Scott says may match or beat 95/96 net.

text.p: Transport group Scott Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it had a reasonable expectation of meeting, if not bettering, its 1995/96 net profit of A$5.2 million, despite a 22 percent fall in the first half of 1996/97.
"There is a reasonable expectation that we will be able to attain last year's results, if not better," managing director Ivan Backman told Reuters.

As it had foreshadowed, Scott earlier on Wednesday reported a 21.8 percent drop in profit after tax for the first half ended December 31 to A$2.8 million, due to restructuring costs, distillate price rises, and a depressed building industry.
Backman said he was hopeful the company would have a reasonably good second half, but could not be optimistic until he saw trading conditions for the three months to March 31.

He said the company's reorganisation was nearly complete and any further costs would be minimal, fuel prices were not rising as significantly, and the company saw some indications of volume improvement in the building industry, he said.
"Restructuring has positioned the group to take advantage of any upwards movement in the economy, particularly the building sector," he said.
"I think we are building up to a better (1997/98)," he said.
Backman said Scott Corp had no acquisition plans in the short-term.
